comment: What he taught in class is SO EASY that never appears in exams. The exams are far harder than the lectures and HW. And he will collect HW at every beginning of class so you cannot miss any class. DO not choose him if you want a pass grade, especially for those new guys in econ.
Doesnt prepare you for tests. Doesnt use technology so you cant see the lectures again if you need extra help

MacKay is a decent professor overall that is open to meet outside of class if you go to his office hours. Personally, I struggled because I'm not naturally inclined to economics or math, and his class is test heavy. His homework is extremely easy but I see this as a disadvantage because it leaves you unprepared for tests.

Definitely a good Micro teacher. Homework takes about five minutes. His lectures are clear. Tests are manageable, but he puts two challenge problems at the end that make them hard. Overall, you can't go wrong with him.
Dr. Mackay is a really good micro professor. He really makes micro an interesting class while he explains thing with clear logic.

He's a good econ teacher. I didn't take an econ class before this and wasn't too confused. He was always available to give help. He gave homework every class but it was never too difficult/time consuming. Tests weren't too bad until the last question or two (I always got those wrong). The entire class is a lecture and he calls on people randomly

I had Dr. Mackay this year for Principles of Microeconomics and had an incredible experience with him. The only grades in the class are the nightly homework (graded on accuracy), two tests,  and a final exam. The tests are somewhat difficult but he will always hold a review session the day before the tests. He also really gets to know his students.

Professor MacKay is overall very clear and makes sure you understand the material before moving on. His class style is he goes around the room and asks everyone a question, so you participate in his class whether you like it or not. Tests are straightforward until you get to the last two questions, which he openly admits you can't really study for.

His homework is easy and the test is straightforward. He really knows his material. But! But! Although his test is straightforward and easy, it is still hard to get an A. Because a tiny mistake can cost a lot. Sometimes it makes you frustrating. It is not an easy A class. But  you don't have to put effort to get a B. Yes, this is annoying.

Good teacher. Homework is easy as it takes 20 minutes or less every class. The tests are straightforward except for the last 1 or 2 questions which tend to be pretty difficult.  He helps you understand the material outside of class but it is only during a small time period each week.

I liked Mackay as a professor. I took Econ in high school and he helped to reinforce the concepts nicely. We had two tests and he screwed up one of them badly, which didn't help my grade. Homework took no longer than 10 minutes usually. Funny guy, tries and fails to get everyones name. Fairly good Micro teacher. Last few test questions were hard.

If you have a lot of free time, Mackay should be good, because his office hours are only once a week, and the review sessions are at the same times. Lectures are good and he makes sure you understand, but he doesn't really offer that many resources to help you study. I took econ before but still found the tests really hard to get a good score on.

His lectures are really good; he answers questions in class if you have them and makes sure you understand. He doesn't offer many resources to review from, except 3 review sessions and past homework. Doesn't use the textbook except for some assignments, which he uploads. Office hours are helpful but only available once a week.

Professor MacKay is fun, engaging and a really good Econ professor. Having said that, his midterms have at least one crazy ass question which will manage to pull your grade down. Apart from that, he's really good at teaching and helping out of class (sometimes he won't help you, i.e., during finals week). If you miss class, you'll lag behind.

MacKay is a good, clear, and funny teacher. If you're not good at econ it can be a difficult class, as he makes his tests kinda hard. But he's straightforward and clear. Don't miss class or you'll fall behind.

MacKay is great if you go to his office hours/ask questions in class. If you don't do this, you may be lost in class. Be prepared to know abstract ideas and apply them to the homework. For the most part he is a generous grader.
The tests are way too long. Ruined my grade

MacKay is one of the best professors I've had here. His lectures aren't boring and he always makes sure everyone in the class understands the topic before he goes on. He's super down to earth and often cracks jokes in class. Doesn't use the textbook at all so taking his class is a great way to save 200 bucks. Tests are entirely note and hw based.

If you want a wonderful beginning for your bschool career, definitely take him! No need to buy a textbook, since he will talk about everything you need to learn during his speech. Tests are not easy, but if you pay attention in class and do the homework, you could get an A.

Two tests are each 20%, homework is another 20% and the final is 40%. Right off the bat, homework is a huge grade inflator as long as you make sure you get it right. Tests are very easy except the last section, which is nearly impossible. This has the effect of curving everyone towards the 80s. The final was a joke. Good teacher, would take again.

Mackay is the man! Save $200 cause he doesn't use the book. His lectures are long but really important. The tests are pretty much the same as the HW so do em and pay attention to when he goes over them. Tests are easy if you pay attention and take good notes. BEST TEACHER FOR ECON 102.

Mackay is the best for econ101. Lectures are super clear, homeworks are easy and tests are not that hard if you understand everything he told in class. I did not take AP econ in high school but I got 90+ in all the exams in this class. Definitely would take him again.

Good teacher, you learn a lot (can't miss class because the book isn't used so everything is learned there). Homework every class but it takes 15 minutes tops. Only problem is that the two tests final are 80% of your grade and they are very difficult. You will be pressed for time and the grading is pretty harsh. Fine for a pretty easy "B" class.

His class is better for those who took eocn before. I have never taken it before and its messed up. Tests are super hard. No textbook requiremen so you dont even know how to prepare for the tests. Never gonna take him  again
Great Professor, great guy!

Pretty much a joke class. If you have taken Econ in high school, he will not cover 50% of the material so you will most likely get an A. I don't know why people are saying he is a "great" professor. If you are considering Econ as a major do not take him, yes you will get the super easy A but chances are you won't learn much

Apparently he's the best econ professor, but that itself is not a very high bar. His lectures get boring, and his tests are super x10 hard, but he's pretty straightfoward. Screws up a lot of people's names.

Mackay is a FANTASTIC professor. He genuinely cares about his students and makes class relevant with examples and stories. He is the best professor I've had at richmond so far and made a very dense topic very understandable. No need to buy the book for 101&102 since he posts the questions online. Loved these classes!

He's the man. I had him for ECON 101 & ECON 102, Lectures are clear, optional textbook (DO NOT buy it), homework is easy and counts for your grade, tests are a bit harder but do-able. He tells the best (uneventful)  stories and is really chill. Overall I spent about 15 min a week on these classes. Take him for both but definitely for Micro -ECON101

He's the man. Your gonna want to take his class. Lectures are clear, optional textbook (DO NOT buy it), homework is easy and counts for your grade, tests are a bit harder but do-able. He tells the best (uneventful)  stories and is really chill. Overall I spent about 15 min a week on these classes. Take him for both but definitely for Micro -ECON101

I got a pretty easy A with maybe studying a total of 7-8 hours all semester long, but I had taken the class before. I would definitely recommend it to someone who hasn't taken Econ101 before though, because he only covers the basics and does not go into depth on other stuff
good professor. clear explanation. not too much homework. test is a little bit hard but the test is comprehensive and helpful. getting A is not very difficult if you study hard.

Really nice guy. He explain things very clearly and he doesn't give out more than 30 minutes of homework a night. His tests are kind of hard but if you study enough you can get an A pretty easily because the tests are pretty straightforward. I would recommend him for ECON 101.
Funny Guy

Mackay is a good professor. His presentation of the material is clear, and he tends to reiterate the concepts, using multiple examples to guarantee understanding. There's homework each class, but it doesn't take more than 15-30 min. He has 2 midterms and a final which aren't that difficult if you grasp the concepts and study. Not a hard A.

Homework takes no more than 10-15 minutes, does not do quizzes but his tests are pretty challenging and usually include at least one concept that he hasn't explained in class but overall he is pretty chill and approachable.

Avoid at all costs. He is unclear and his tests are nothing like you learn in class. he throws tons of formulas at you and doesn't teach you how to use them in the ways he tests you on. he doesn't follow the textbook- in fact says that it teaches wrong,  so you have to rely on his teaching during class or help from other students

Mackay is the worst teacher I have ever had. He spends all class jumping from topic to topic and does not show you how to use the equations he teaches. You can spend all the time you like studying the information but just know you will be asked something completely new on the Exam. This class tests your ability to interpret his wording, not stats.

Professor Mackay is very nice and caring. He is very patient and approachable. Although he is very smart, he is not that good at teaching the material. There are 3 exams which tend to me much harder then a material covered in class. Not an easy A, but I would still recommend him.
B Stats is boring, but Dr. Mackay really cared about us learning which made me want to do well.  He was available for extra help, was funny and patient.

Professor Mackay is a smart guy; however, it business statistics, he does not know how to teach correctly... there were 2 tests all semester, and most people did poorly because it's difficult to understand his wording... the final is worth 40% of your grade....oh, and he can't spell! DO NOT SUFFER AS I HAVE!

Great prof, and easily the best Micro teacher to take. He's straight forward, pretty easy going, focuses on the concepts and doesn't give a ton of homework. The tests are difficult, but it evens out with the amount of homework given. He's a really cool guy and easy to learn from!

such a good professor! i would recommend him to anyone. he is totally fair and always willing to help with whatever you may need. really cares about how you are doing in his class and wants you to do well. tests are kind of difficult but if you attend class and pay attention you will be fine. homework grade also helps! plus he's a really funny dude
Tests are not hard as long as you study and know the information. Homework is always pretty easy- only a few short questions. He's a pretty chill guy- I recommend him for Micro.

Prof MacKay was a very straightforward teacher.  At first I thought that he just repeated himself over and over again in class, but then I realized by the end of the course I had learned everything need to do well on the exams without really studying.  Short homework, never uses the book.  You will learn in this class w/out much effort. take him

Prof. Mackay gives short, straight forward homework assignments almost every class and has 3 big exams. The exams can be challenging, but he offers review sessions, and he is good at explaining and answering questions when they are presented.

As long as you take notes in class and take time to do the homework correctly based off of the notes in class you should do well. The tests can be relatively easy as long as you study a good amount and understand the material. He makes a lot of corny jokes... I thought he was funny though. I would recommend his class.

I actually enjoyed his class very much.He knows what he is talking about and how to portray to his students.Very helpful in class and if you go to his office hours.Homework daily (but it is easy and only 1-2 questions).2 tests& then final which are pretty simple if you read and follow all the directions. dont use the book at all really.take him!

I honestly hated this course. Maybe it's just I don't like econ in general, but I didn't think he was a very good professor either. He doesn't use the text book, and rushes through lectures. He is also a hard grader. There are 2 exams and 1 final, and he assigns homework assignments for every class. Overall the class is just very dry and difficult.
